families.summary: Sonix Health is a software-only echocardiography analysis workstation from Ontact Health (Seoul) that classifies views and produces semi-automated 2D, M-mode and Doppler measurements per ASE guidelines for user review. K230209 (2023) cleared 18 views and a core measurement set; K240645 (2024) expanded to 36 views and added Auto-Strain (LV GLS/segmental strain, LA reservoir/contraction strain, RV free-wall strain) plus additional RV, M-mode and derived measurements.
families.intended_use_quote:
Sonix Health is intended for quantifying and reporting echocardiography for use by or on the order of a licensed physician. Sonix Health accepts DICOM-compliant medical images acquired from ultrasound imaging devices. Sonix Health is indicated for use in adult populations.

Ultrasound images are acquired via the B (2D), M, Pulsed-wave Doppler, and Continuous-wave Doppler modes.
families.indications_for_use_quote:

embedded_ai_features: Two-step deep learning: single view-identification model, then view-specific B-mode / M-mode / Doppler segmentation models
Semi-automated view classification (18 views in K230209; 36 views in K240645)
Semi-automated 2D, M-mode and Doppler measurements with user review/edit
Auto-Strain: LVGLS, segmental longitudinal strain, LA reservoir and contraction strain, RV free-wall strain (K240645)
Derived indices: EF (Teichholz and MOD), RWT, SV, LV mass, %FS, RV FAC, TAPSE (K240645)
Report generation

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Predicate TOMTEC-ARENA (K213544); reference device Samsung Medison V8 Diagnostic Ultrasound System (K220975). 18 semi-automated views and 2D/M-mode/Doppler measurement set.

Predicate is prior Sonix Health (K230209); reference devices EchoPAC Software Only/Plug-in (K220940) and TOMTEC-ARENA (K213544). View classification expanded from 18 to 36 views (adds PLAX zoomed views, A3C, A5C, PSAX levels, subcostal, RV-focused A4C, M-mode TAPSE, TDI septal/lateral/tricuspid). Adds Auto-Strain (LVGLS/LVSLS, LARS, LACtS, RVFWS), RV dimensions/areas/FAC, Teichholz EF/volumes, LV mass, %FS, RWT, LVOT (2D). Same intended use and indications.

training_data.description: K230209 summary: training data collected from six centers; representative institution demographics 50.2% male, mean BMI 22.2, mean LVEF 67.0%. Training set size not stated. Both summaries state training and validation data are distinct and independent. Peer-reviewed papers from Ontact Health describe development on a 'nationwide echocardiographic dataset from five tertiary hospitals' (e.g., M-mode model trained on 5,958 M-mode images), but those papers do not name Sonix Health explicitly.

validation_data.description: K230209: 2,744 test images (476 B-mode, 243 M-mode, 2,025 Doppler) from one U.S. hospital (1,264) and one South Korean hospital (1,384), four equipment manufacturers, LVEF 14-76%. K240645: images from 335 patients (Mayo Clinic Arizona and Severance Hospital, Seoul); n_patients here refers to the K240645 test set; K230209 reports images, not patients.

prior_validations.description: Korea Biomedical Review (2026-05-06) reports company-stated performance for SONIX HEALTH: B-mode image classification 96% accuracy, Doppler 99%, M-mode 100%, LV GLS correlation ~0.97; 'one-click' analysis reducing examination time by more than 70%; in use at about 3,000 medical institutions worldwide as of end 2025; Samjin Pharmaceutical exclusive Korea distribution MOU. Also states MFDS Class II certification.

Ontact Health-affiliated papers validate the group's automated view identification and measurement pipeline: M-mode automation (PMID 38652399), diastolic function automation (PMID 38975004), STEMI cohort of 632 patients (PMID 39434367), and a prospective 40-exam workflow pilot showing LVEF noninferiority (PMID 42157304). Product name not stated in abstracts.

papers.title: Fully automated quantification of cardiac chamber and function assessment in 2-D echocardiography: clinical feasibility of deep learning-based algorithms
papers.key_result: Yonsei CONNECT-AI / Mayo Clinic Arizona group (same institutions as Sonix Health validation sites); 500 consecutive TTE patients; U-Net variants achieved average Dice 0.91-0.95 for four-chamber segmentation with no significant differences in LAV, LVEDV, LVESV, LV mass or EF vs ground truth. Does not name Sonix Health; predates clearance.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced automation for M-mode echocardiographic analysis: ensuring fully automated, reliable, and reproducible measurements
papers.key_result: Ontact Health-affiliated. Developed on 5,958 M-mode images from five tertiary hospitals; view classification accuracy 99.8%, segmentation Dice 94.3%; internal test (100 images) PCC 0.81-0.99 vs experts; external test (280 images) PCC 0.84-0.98 (sinus rhythm) and 0.70-0.97 (AF). Product not named in abstract.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enhanced automation of left ventricular diastolic assessment: a pilot study for feasibility, diagnostic validation, and outcome prediction
papers.key_result: Ontact Health-affiliated. External validation at Seoul National University Bundang Hospital (200 exams): view identification accuracy 99.1%; AI vs manual diastolic parameters Pearson 0.901-0.959; 94% concordance in guideline LVDF grading; AI-derived grades prognostic (adjusted HR 3.03). Product not named in abstract.

papers.title: An Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Echocardiographic Analysis: Enhancing Efficiency and Prognostic Evaluation in Patients With Revascularized STEMI
papers.key_result: Ontact Health-affiliated. 632 STEMI patients; view identification accuracy 98.5%; AI vs manual LVEF, GLS, LAVI and LA reservoir strain Pearson 0.81-0.92, ICC 0.74-0.90; AI measurements prognostic independent of clinical risk factors. Product not named in abstract.

papers.title: Novel deep learning framework for simultaneous assessment of left ventricular mass and longitudinal strain: clinical feasibility and validation in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
papers.key_result: Ontact Health-affiliated SMART (segmentation-based myocardial tracking) framework for automated LV mass and LVGLS; comparable LVGLS and more accurate LVM than conventional TTE in HCM. Product not named in abstract.

papers.title: Fully automated artificial intelligence-based echocardiographic analysis substantially reduces workflow time while preserving measurement accuracy: a pilot study
papers.key_result: Ontact Health-affiliated prospective single-center pilot, 40 TTE exams: median analysis time 94 s (AI) vs 490 s (sonographer), P<0.001; AI LVEF noninferior to cardiologist-adjudicated reference (mean difference 0.00 points, upper 95% bound 1.41; ICC 0.902); secondary index ICCs 0.625-0.989. Product not named in abstract.

papers.title: Reinventing the echocardiography workflow: from manual quantification to artificial intelligence-driven comprehensive interpretation
papers.key_result: Review by Ontact Health-affiliated authors (incl. CEO Hyuk-Jae Chang) on AI echo workflow.

open_questions: Training set size (number of studies/patients) is not stated in either FDA summary; only 'six centers' and representative-institution demographics are given.
K230209 summary reports images, not patient counts, for the test set; number of patients unknown.
K240645 summary's site breakdown is internally inconsistent (303 American/32 Korean vs 93 U.S./200 Korean); actual per-site counts unresolved.
Per-measurement agreement statistics (Bland-Altman bias/LoA) and subgroup analyses are stated to be in labeling, not in the summary.
No paper explicitly names 'Sonix Health' in PubMed abstracts; linkage of Ontact Health-affiliated papers to the cleared device is by affiliation and methodology, not by explicit statement.
sonixhealth.ai product pages could not be parsed (JS-rendered); company-page deployment details beyond the FDA summary (on-premise PC, local network) unverified.
Korea Biomedical Review performance figures (96/99/100% classification accuracy, GLS r~0.97, ~3,000 institutions) are company statements reported in news; not verified against a primary source.

families.summary: EchoMeasure (iCardio.ai, Los Angeles) processes previously acquired DICOM TTE studies, classifies views, checks image quality, identifies ED/ES frames, and outputs ten automated linear and volumetric measurements (LV volumes A2C/A4C/biplane, LV and RV diameters, wall thicknesses, aortic annulus, LVOT, sinus of Valsalva, sinotubular junction, LA dimension). Output is intended for consumption by third-party software; users can accept or reject but not edit results. Cleared 2024-10-10 (K241430) with Libby Echo:Prio (K220956) as predicate.
families.intended_use_quote: Quantification of cardiovascular function from an echocardiogram
families.indications_for_use_quote:
iCardio.ai EchoMeasure is software that is used to process previously acquired DICOM-compliant cardiac ultrasound images, and to make measurements on these images in order to provide automated estimation of several cardiac measurements. The data produced by this software is intended to be used to support qualified cardiologists, sonographers, or other licensed professional healthcare practitioners for clinical decision-making.

iCardio.ai EchoMeasure is indicated for use in adult patients.
embedded_ai_features: Machine-learning view classification
Image quality grading
End-diastolic / end-systolic frame identification
Automated keypoint detection and segmentation

Ten automated measurements: LV volume (A2C, A4C, biplane; systole/diastole), LV diameter (systole/diastole), RV diameter, posterior wall thickness, aortic annulus, LVOT diameter, sinus of Valsalva, sinotubular junction, LA dimension, IVS thickness
Contours/keypoints overlaid on images; user confirmation/rejection (no manual editing)
Automated report (browser interface, PDF)

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Predicate Libby Echo:Prio (K220956). Differences vs predicate: adds image-quality checks and ten linear/volumetric measurements instead of EF; removes manual editing of automated results; output intended for third-party software consumption.

families.summary: CardioVision (iCardio.ai) is a CNN-based decision-support tool that analyzes a single PLAX cine-loop DICOM and outputs a binary 'none/mild' vs 'moderate/severe' aortic stenosis classification (or 'indeterminate' for poor image quality), intended as a diagnostic aid in outpatient settings for adults over 21. Cleared 2025-11-21 (K251293, product code QUO, 21 CFR 870.2200) with EchoGo Heart Failure (K222463) as predicate. Standalone validation: 650 studies from 608 subjects at 12 U.S. sites; AUROC 0.945, sensitivity 0.896, specificity 0.872.
families.intended_use_quote: Providing adjunctive information on a patient’s cardiovascular condition (diagnostic aid for aortic stenosis).
families.indications_for_use_quote:
The iCardio.ai CardioVision™ AI is an automated machine learning–based decision support system, indicated as a diagnostic aid for patients undergoing an echocardiographic exam consisting of a single PLAX view in an outpatient environment, such as a primary care setting.

When utilized by an interpreting clinician, this device provides information that may be useful in detecting moderate or severe aortic stenosis. iCardio.ai CardioVision™ AI is indicated in adult populations over 21 years of age. Patient management decisions should not be made solely on the results of the iCardio.ai CardioVision™ AI analysis. iCardio.ai CardioVision™ AI analyzes a single cine-loop DICOM of the parasternal long axis (PLAX).
embedded_ai_features: Set of convolutional neural networks estimating likelihood of moderate or severe aortic stenosis from a single PLAX cine loop
Binary output none/mild vs moderate/severe; 'indeterminate' output for insufficient image quality
Auto view classification (accepts partial or full study containing at least one PLAX view with a full cardiac cycle)
Fixed (locked) models; pre/post-processing for PACS, DICOM viewer and worklist integration

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Predicate EchoGo Heart Failure 1.0 (Ultromics, K222463, QUO). Primary difference is the condition assessed (aortic stenosis vs HFpEF) and input (single PLAX loop vs A4C); adds auto-view classification; indicated for adults over 21 (predicate over 25).

reviewed by OHT2 Office of Cardiovascular Devices

papers.title: Automated Detection of Aortic Stenosis Using Machine Learning
papers.key_result: Tufts / iCardio.ai. CNNs for view identification and study-level AS grading trained on 338 patients, validated on 119, tested on 120: AUROC 0.96 for screening, 0.86 for no-significant vs significant (moderate/severe) AS; external validation in 8,502 outpatient TTEs showed PLAX-only AS screening AUROC 0.91. Cited by iCardio.ai as the CardioVision publication.

papers.title: Automated Detection of Clinically Significant Mitral Regurgitation from Single-View B-Mode Echocardiography Using Deep Learning
papers.key_result: iCardio.ai 'MitralVision' (not the cleared CardioVision AS device): trained on 28,487 A4C loops from 11,244 studies across 20 U.S. states; external validation on 629 studies from 26 sites AUROC 0.91, sensitivity 82.1%, specificity 84.3%. Included as evidence of the company's single-view valvular pipeline; not a CardioVision validation.

families.summary: Libby Echo:Prio (Dyad Medical, Boston) is browser-based, machine-learning echocardiography post-processing software that classifies views (PLAX, PSAX, A4C, A5C, A2C, A3C), identifies ED/ES frames with heart-rate estimation, segments LV endocardium, LA and LV myocardium, and produces a fully automated single-plane and biplane ejection fraction that the sonographer can accept, edit or reject. Cleared 2022-07-20 (K220956) with Bay Labs EchoMD AutoEF (K173780) as predicate; later served as the predicate for iCardio.ai EchoMeasure (K241430).
families.indications_for_use_quote:
Libby Echo:Prio is software that is used to process previously acquired DICOM-compliant cardiac ultrasound images, and to make measurements on these images in order to provide automated estimation of several cardiac measurements. The data produced by this software is intended to be used to support qualified cardiologists, sonographers, or other licensed professional healthcare practitioners for clinical decision-making.

Libby Echo:Prio is indicated for use in adult patients.
embedded_ai_features: Machine-learning echocardiographic view classification (PLAX, PSAX, A4C, A5C, A2C, A3C)
End-diastole / end-systole frame identification enabling heart-rate estimate
Automated LV endocardium, LA and LV myocardium segmentation
Fully automated ejection fraction (single plane and biplane) including clip selection
Qualitative user feedback on image quality
Manual markup/correction and report generation

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance. Predicate EchoMD Automated Ejection Fraction Software (Bay Labs, K173780). Differences: browser-based UI vs PC/PACS; segmentation-based single-plane and biplane EF vs non-segmentation biplane EF; qualitative (not quantitative) image-quality feedback.

performance_claims.quote: Finally, the prediction of the EF output using the Libby™ Echo:Prio software had a slope of 0.79 for Bivariate Linear Regression (BLS) with the 95% confidence interval (CI) of (0.52, 0.98) compared with the annotations by four human experts. This is well within the range of typical measurement variation between different clinicians, which is usually described as inter-observer variation and can be as low as (0.37, 0.52) of the 95% CI.

notes: All five FDA summaries read in full. Performance numbers are quoted verbatim with the 'PAGE n' index from the extracted text files. Dates and product codes taken from openfda_records.json. Papers were resolved via PubMed E-utilities and Crossref in this session; Ontact Health-affiliated papers do not name Sonix Health in their abstracts, so linkage is by affiliation/methodology. No PubMed papers were found for EchoMeasure or Libby Echo:Prio. CardioVision's Breakthrough Device status is company-reported only. ClinicalTrials.gov searches for iCardio, Ontact Health, Sonix Health, Dyad Medical and Libby Echo returned no relevant registrations. Company/news performance figures (Korea Biomedical Review for Sonix Health) are kept out of performance_claims and recorded under prior_validations.
